title: Torque, equilibrium, and center of mass
summary: How does a force cause rotation, and when does an object stay balanced or tip over?
cards.0.p: The turning effect of a force is called torque, given by τ = F·d. Here d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force, and it is called the lever arm. With a longer arm, less force is enough.
cards.0.key: Torque is also called the moment of a force. For the same torque, a longer lever arm needs less force (F = τ / d).
cards.1.p: If the force makes an angle θ with r, the lever arm is d = r·sinθ, and τ = F·r·sinθ. The component perpendicular to r does the turning. sin90° = 1 and sin0° = 0.
cards.1.svg#7: if the line passes through O, d = 0 and τ = 0
cards.1.key: sin30° = sin150° = 0.5. The component F·cosθ along r produces no torque. A force whose line passes through the pivot does not turn the object either.
cards.1.etk.soru: Change the force, the distance, and the angle. What happens to the torque when θ = 0° or 180°?
cards.2.p: A torque turns an object clockwise or counterclockwise. Choose one direction as + and give the other −. The net torque is the sum of the signed torques.
cards.2.key: Most books take counterclockwise as +. Decide the directions before you add torques. Opposite torques are subtracted from each other.
cards.2.once.soru: A torque of 30 N·m clockwise and 20 N·m counterclockwise act on a bar. What is the net torque, in N·m?
cards.2.once.secenekler.0.neden: Opposite torques are subtracted: 30 − 20 = 10 N·m, clockwise.
cards.2.once.secenekler.1.neden: Opposite torques do not add up, they are subtracted.
cards.2.once.secenekler.2.neden: If the torques were equal, the total would be zero. But 30 and 20 are not equal.
cards.3.h: Unit: N·m, but not the joule
cards.3.p: The unit of torque is the N·m. The joule is also N·m, but in work the force is multiplied by the distance along the same line, and in torque by the perpendicular distance. So torque is not written in joules.
cards.3.key: Torque is given in N·m. The joule is used only for work and energy.
cards.3.once.soru: Which is the unit of torque?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: Torque is force times perpendicular distance. Its unit is the newton times the meter.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: The joule is for work and energy. Torque is written in N·m.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: The newton is the unit of force. In torque the force is multiplied by a distance.
cards.4.p: Equilibrium needs two conditions: ΣF = 0 for translation and Στ = 0 for rotation. Two equal and opposite forces along different lines are called a couple, and a couple turns the object.
cards.4.key: In equilibrium Στ = 0 holds about every point. So you can choose the pivot wherever it suits you.
cards.5.h: A bar and its support forces
cards.5.p: Put the pivot on one support, so that the torque of that support is zero. The weight of a uniform bar acts at its midpoint. The equation ΣF = 0 then gives the other support.
cards.5.key: Take a 4 m bar weighing 40 N with a 60 N load 1 m from A. About A, N₂·4 = 40·2 + 60·1, so N₂ = 35 N. From ΣF = 0, N₁ = 65 N.
cards.6.p: To find the tension in a rope holding a hinged bar, take torques about the hinge, because the torque of the hinge force is zero. The torque of the rope is T·L·sinα, and the torque of the bar is W·L/2.
cards.6.key: The tension depends on the angle the rope makes with the bar. The smaller the angle, the larger T.
cards.6.once.soru: The end of a 100 N horizontal bar hinged to a wall is held by a rope at 30° to the bar. What is the tension in the rope, in N?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: About the hinge, T·L·sin30° = 100·L/2. This gives T = 100 N.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: The weight acts at the middle, but the rope pulls at an angle. So sin30° = 0.5 comes into it.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: The weight of the bar acts at its middle, not at its end.
cards.7.h: Center of mass and center of gravity
cards.7.p: The center of mass is the point where an object behaves as if all its mass were there. In uniform gravity the weight also acts at this point, which is called the center of gravity. For a ring this point is in empty space.
cards.7.key: For a uniform object the center of mass lies on the axis or center of symmetry.
cards.7.once.soru: Where is the center of mass of a uniform ring?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: A ring is symmetric. Its center of mass is at the geometric center, even though there is no material there.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: Every point of the ring is symmetric, and no point stands out.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.yazi: It has no center of mass
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: Every object has a center of mass.
cards.8.h: Center of mass of a composite object
cards.8.p: For an object made of parts, the center of mass is xCM = Σm·x / Σm. The center of mass is closer to the heavier part. A part that has been removed counts as a negative mass.
cards.8.key: If a 3 kg part is at x = 0 and a 1 kg part is at x = 4 m, then xCM = (0 + 4) / 4 = 1 m.
cards.9.h: Base of support and tipping over
cards.9.p: If the vertical line down from the center of gravity falls inside the base of support, the object does not tip over. If it falls outside, the object tips. A low center of gravity and a wide base make tipping harder.
cards.9.svg#4: vertical line from the center of gravity
cards.9.key: The tipping limit is the moment the vertical line through the center of gravity passes exactly through the edge of the base. That is why race cars are low.
cards.10.p: A box on an incline slides when tanα > μs and tips when tanα > b/h (b is the base, h is the height). As the angle grows, whichever limit is reached first happens.
cards.10.key: If μs < b/h, the box slides without tipping; if μs > b/h, it tips without sliding.
cards.10.svg#5: the line is still inside the base: no tipping
cards.10.once.soru: You put a low box with a wide base on an icy ramp. If the ramp slowly gets steeper, what does the box do first?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: On ice there is very little friction, so the sliding limit is reached early. For a low box to tip, the ramp would have to be very steep.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: A low box has a low center of gravity. The ramp would have to get very steep for it to tip.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: There is little friction on ice. The box starts to move as soon as the ramp gets a bit steeper.
cards.11.p: If an object returns after a small push, its equilibrium is stable. If it moves away, it is unstable. If it stays in its new place, it is neutral. In stable equilibrium the center of gravity is at its lowest.
cards.11.svg#9: push the ball a little: what happens?
cards.11.key: A ball in a hollow is in stable equilibrium, a ball on a hilltop is unstable, and a ball on flat ground is neutral. After a push, the center of gravity rises in the stable case and drops in the unstable case.
cards.11.etk.soru: What happens after a small push? Choose the type of equilibrium.
cards.11.etk.ogeler.0.0: Ball at the bottom of a hollow
cards.11.etk.ogeler.2.0: Ruler hung from its top end
cards.11.etk.ogeler.2.2: When pushed, the center of gravity rises, and the ruler swings back.
cards.11.etk.ogeler.3.0: Ball on top of a hill
cards.11.etk.ogeler.4.2: When pushed, the center of gravity drops, and the pencil falls.
cards.11.etk.ogeler.6.2: As it rolls, the center of gravity stays at the same height.
cards.11.etk.ogeler.7.0: Wheel mounted on an axle at its center
cards.11.etk.ogeler.7.2: As it turns, the center of gravity does not move.
cards.11.once.soru: You give a small push to a ball at the bottom of a hollow. What happens?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: When pushed, the ball rises. Its weight pulls it back to the lowest point.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: A ball on a hilltop would move away. A ball in a hollow cannot climb out.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.yazi: It stays in its new place
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: A ball on flat ground would do that. In a hollow the ground rises toward the edges.
cards.12.p:
• Torque is τ = F·d = F·r·sinθ, and its unit is N·m. Its direction is clockwise or counterclockwise.
• Equilibrium needs both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0.
• The weight of a uniform bar acts at its middle.
• The center of mass is xCM = Σm·x / Σm.
• If the vertical line falls outside the base, the object tips over.
quiz.0.q: A 50 N force is applied to the end of a 0.4 m wrench at an angle of 30° to the wrench. What is the torque about the nut, in N·m?
quiz.0.e: τ = F·r·sinθ = 50·0.4·0.5 = 10 N·m. If the force were perpendicular to the wrench, the torque would be 20 N·m.
quiz.1.q: What happens after a small push? Choose the type of equilibrium for each object.
quiz.1.ogeler.1.0: Picture hung on a nail from its top
quiz.1.ogeler.3.0: Broom balanced upright on a finger
quiz.1.ogeler.5.0: Ruler on an axle through its center of mass
quiz.1.e: When a cone on its base or a hanging picture is pushed, the center of gravity rises and the object returns. These are in stable equilibrium. When a cone on its tip or an upright broom is pushed, the center of gravity drops and the object falls. These are in unstable equilibrium. When a cone on its side rolls or a ruler on an axle turns, the height of the center of gravity does not change. These are in neutral equilibrium.
quiz.2.q: A force is applied to a hinged bar. r is the distance from the hinge to the point where the force acts. Put the torques in order from smallest to largest.
quiz.2.ogeler.0: 20 N, r = 0.5 m, line of action through the hinge
quiz.2.ogeler.1: 20 N, r = 0.8 m, at 30° to the bar
quiz.2.ogeler.2: 20 N, r = 0.5 m, perpendicular to the bar
quiz.2.ogeler.3: 30 N, r = 0.6 m, perpendicular to the bar
quiz.2.e: Use τ = F·r·sinθ. For the force whose line passes through the hinge, τ = 0. The others are 20·0.8·0.5 = 8, 20·0.5 = 10, and 30·0.6 = 18 N·m.
quiz.3.q: A 6 m uniform bar weighing 120 N is supported at its ends A and B. A 300 N load is 2 m from end A. What force, in N, does support B exert on the bar?
quiz.3.e: Taking torques about A, N<sub>B</sub>·6 = 120·3 + 300·2 = 960, so N<sub>B</sub> = 160 N. From ΣF = 0, N<sub>A</sub> = 420 − 160 = 260 N.
A:baslik: Torque, equilibrium, and center of mass
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Push the door, balance the seesaw, hang the bar, and tip the box.
A:adimlar.0.metin: The turning effect, or torque, is the force times the distance from the hinge. Opening this door takes a torque of 12 N·m. Put your hand where 20 N is enough.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: At d = 0.6 m, F = 12 / 0.6 = 20 N is enough, and farther out even less will do. If you push 0.2 m from the hinge, you need 60 N.
A:adimlar.1.metin: You apply a 20 N force to the end of a wrench, at a distance r = 0.5 m from the nut. Change the angle between the force and the wrench and make the torque as large as possible.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: At θ = 90°, τ = 20 · 0.5 · 1 = 10 N·m. When the force is perpendicular to the wrench, the lever arm is longest (d = r).
A:adimlar.2.baslik: When the line passes through the hinge
A:adimlar.2.metin: You apply 20 N to a door 0.8 m from the hinge. But the line of the force passes right through the hinge.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: What is the torque on the door, in N·m?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: If the force were perpendicular to the door, the torque would be 20 · 0.8 = 16. But what is the lever arm here?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A force whose line passes through the pivot has a lever arm d = 0, so τ = 0. However hard you push, the door does not turn. You only press on the hinge.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: 20 / 0.8 = 25, but torque comes from the product F·d, not from a division.
A:adimlar.3.metin: The 300 N child on the left is 2 m from the pivot. At balance the torques in the two directions are equal. Seat the 400 N child where the seesaw stays balanced.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: 400 · 1.5 = 600 N·m, which equals 300 · 2. The opposite torques are equal, so Στ = 0. The heavier child sits closer to the pivot. Ignoring the weight of the board, the pivot pushes up with 700 N, so ΣF = 0.
A:adimlar.4.metin: A 4 m uniform bar weighing 40 N is supported at both ends, and its weight acts at its middle. Slide the 60 N load and make the force carried by support B 65 N.
A:adimlar.4.kontroller.0.etiket: Distance of the load from A
A:adimlar.4.gorev.tamam: About A, N<sub>B</sub> · 4 = 40 · 2 + 60 · 3, so N<sub>B</sub> = 65 N. From ΣF = 0, N<sub>A</sub> = 100 − 65 = 35 N. The closer the load is to B, the more B carries.
A:adimlar.5.metin: A light bar has 2 kg at its left end and a mass at its right end, 4 m away. You hang the bar from the point at 3 m. Change the mass on the right and make the bar hang level.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: x<sub>CM</sub> = (2·0 + 6·4) / (2 + 6) = 3 m. A bar hung from its center of mass stays balanced. The center of mass is closer to the heavier part.
A:adimlar.6.metin: You put two boxes with the same base on a rough board that tilts slowly. The boxes do not slide.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The low box has a low center of gravity. So its vertical line does not easily leave the base.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Their bases are the same, but their centers of gravity are at different heights.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The tall box has a high center of gravity. At about 22° its vertical line leaves the base and the box tips over. The low box holds out until 45°.
A:kapanis.0: Torque is τ = F·d = F·r·sinθ, and its unit is N·m. The lever arm d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of the force.
A:kapanis.1: A force whose line passes through the pivot has zero torque. The largest torque comes at θ = 90°.
A:kapanis.2: Equilibrium needs both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0. The weight of a uniform bar acts at its middle.
A:kapanis.3: The center of mass is x<sub>CM</sub> = Σm·x / Σm, and it is closer to the heavier part.
A:kapanis.4: If the vertical line from the center of gravity falls outside the base, the object tips over. A low center of gravity and a wide base make tipping harder.
